verses.text: Of David. Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.

xrefs.text: The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song.
The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
“Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.”

verses.text: Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.

xrefs.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns.
Put an end to the evil of the wicked, but establish the righteous, O righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
You have tried my heart; You have visited me in the night. You have tested me and found no evil; I have resolved not to sin with my mouth.

This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold. They will call on My name, and I will answer them. I will say, ‘They are My people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is our God.’”
For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver.

verses.text: For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.

xrefs.text: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.
“Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.
I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.

verses.text: I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites.

xrefs.text: I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them. Because Your hand was on me, I sat alone, for You have filled me with indignation.
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
“Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may obey the commandments of my God.

verses.text: I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked.

xrefs.text: I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but in the LORD I trust.
I will set no worthless thing before my eyes. I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me.
Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

verses.text: I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD,

xrefs.text: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!
He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
with which Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet.
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.

verses.text: to raise my voice in thanksgiving and declare all Your wonderful works.

xrefs.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Death of the Son.” A Psalm of David. I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will recount all Your wonders.
O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.
the glorious splendor of Your majesty. And I will meditate on Your wondrous works.
Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; tell of all His wonders.
Lift up your hands to the sanctuary and bless the LORD!

verses.text: O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides.

xrefs.text: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.
One thing I have asked of the LORD; this is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and seek Him in His temple.
For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your prosperity.

verses.text: Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed,

xrefs.text: O God, that You would slay the wicked— away from me, you bloodthirsty men—
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by its gates.
All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.
Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.text: in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes.

xrefs.text: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside toward dishonest gain, accepting bribes and perverting justice.
Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.

verses.text: But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me.

xrefs.text: Of David. Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes.
For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life you inherited from your forefathers,
saying, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, righteous, and blameless our conduct was among you who believed.

verses.text: My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD.

xrefs.text: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of my oppressors.
He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm.
He guards the steps of His faithful ones, but the wicked perish in darkness; for by his own strength shall no man prevail.
Hallelujah! I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart in the council of the upright and in the assembly.
I will proclaim Your name to my brothers; I will praise You in the assembly.
